measurements.notes: Not an RQ3 metric. Recorded so the verification numbers can be reported either as 'what a verifier costs end to end' or as 'what the verification work costs', without re-running anything.

includes: keccak-256 + secp256k1 self-test vectors (run on every verifier invocation)
bundle parse, canonical serialisation, credential digests, snapshot digest, Merkle root
ES256K-R JWS verification per credential (key recovered from the signature — no network)
measurements.notes: Verdict INCOMPLETE is expected and correct: with --offline every network-dependent check SKIPs. Design A's ES256K-R signatures DO verify in this mode — the issuer key is recovered from the signature itself, so no network is needed to check them; what --offline forgoes is chain state (DID liveness, the authorization root, the anchor event).

includes: contract execution with cold storage slots (vm.coolSlot before each call)
measurements.notes: NOT what a relayer pays — see gas.totalTx. Kept because it is the committed, machine-readable artifact and it isolates contract design from transaction overhead: `anchor` writes no storage beyond its nonce, which is why its execution cost is a third of claimProduct's.

measurements.metric: Gas — vollständige Transaktion (was der Relayer zahlt)
excludes: gas price — deliberately a separate, timestamped row (see gas.price)
measurements.notes: `anchor` is the RECURRING per-publish cost; claimProduct and setIssuer are one-off per product and per authorised issuer. More than 60 % of `anchor` is calldata plus the flat transaction fee rather than execution — the event-log design paying off against a storage-based anchor (~20 000 gas more).

includes: a single eth_gasPrice observation per endpoint, at the timestamp in provenance.takenAt
excludes: any averaging over time — one observation is one observation
measurements.notes: A SPOT price, not a distribution: repeating eth_gasPrice would measure the endpoint's oracle, not the market. Gas units are deterministic and belong in gas.totalTx; this row is the volatile half and must be re-quoted with its timestamp. Mainnet is null unless --mainnet-rpc is given — §13 asks for 'Amoy + Mainnet', and the gas UNITS are identical on both (same bytecode, same calldata); only price differs.

includes: real gasUsed and the real effectiveGasPrice actually paid, from the mined receipts
excludes: anything recurring — this is paid once per chain, ever
measurements.notes: The only Design A gas figures in this report that come from transactions that REALLY HAPPENED. They are also a cross-check on the instrument: these receipts must agree with contracts/README.md.

measurements.metric: Gas — reale Zeremonie-Transaktionen (claimProduct / setIssuer / anchor, gasUsed aus Receipts)
measurements.reason: no claimProduct, setIssuer or anchor transaction has been submitted to Amoy — the AnchorTx outbox is empty
measurements.precondition: one Design A publication driven end to end: brand claims the product, authorises issuers, and the relayer drains one anchor to a confirmed receipt
measurements.notes: Until then gas.totalTx (Foundry, cold slots, corroborated by a local-node cast send) is the defensible figure. contracts/README.md records that a real cast send matched it exactly for claimProduct and anchor, and to within 12 gas for setIssuer — signature bytes differ per key and a zero calldata byte costs 4 gas against 16, so the live figure moves slightly.

includes: measured gas units × the gas price observed at provenance.takenAt
excludes: any claim that this price will hold — gas price is volatile and this is one observation
measurements.notes: Paid by the platform relayer and re-billed in euros (§19 gas abstraction). No supply-chain actor and no brand ever holds POL — the only funded wallet in the system is the platform treasury.

measurements.reason: no POL/USD rate was supplied, and this harness deliberately does not fetch one — a rate scraped from a price API at run time is unciteable and irreproducible in a thesis
measurements.precondition: --pol-usd <rate>, with a source and a date the thesis can cite

measurements.notes: Exactly zero, and known by construction rather than by measurement: a did:ethr identifier is DERIVED from the address (did:ethr:<chain>:0x…), so it exists the moment a key exists. ERC-1056 is consulted only for CHANGES (rotation, delegation, revocation); an unchanged DID has no registry entry and needs no transaction. This is the row that makes §24's onboarding claim affordable, so it is stated as a design property rather than smuggled in as a measured 0.

measurements.reason: Design B touches no chain at all. Plain B — the deployed status quo (§15) — signs centrally and does not anchor, so there is no transaction to price. Reporting '0' here would be a FALSE EQUIVALENCE: it would read as 'Design B does the same thing for free' rather than 'Design B does not do this'.

includes: outbox queue wait (nextTryAt scheduling, relayer poll interval)
Polygon block time and the relayer's confirmation depth
excludes: the publish itself — the clock starts when the AnchorTx row is created
measurements.notes: Read from stored timestamps, NOT re-measured by polling: polling would measure this harness's poll interval rather than the system's. Note this is dominated by the relayer's scheduling policy, which is an implementation choice, not a property of the chain.

measurements.reason: the tKey ceremony is browser-side (OAuth redirect, 2-of-3 share reconstruction, key derivation in the page) and Phase 4 identity — Web3Auth login, wallet-login endpoints, org wallet binding — is not shipped
measurements.precondition: Phase 4 complete, plus ONE of: (a) the frontend emitting performance marks at login-start and did-bound, which this harness would read; or (b) a headless browser driving the real login. (b) is the defensible one — it times what a user actually waits for.
measurements.notes: §7 and §24 claim 30–60 s. That is an ESTIMATE and is currently unverified. It is also the single most load-bearing number in the onboarding argument (the Minespider failure was an onboarding failure), so it should not ship as an estimate.

measurements.reason: not run: this measurement MUTATES (each run creates an organization), so it is opt-in
measurements.notes: §24 estimates 10–30 s for Design B. Note that the technical portion — did:web document plus a platform-held signing key — is server-side and fast; most of the estimate is human form-filling, which is the same in both designs and therefore not the discriminating quantity.

measurements.reason: Design B actors never sign. The platform signs the whole graph centrally at publish time with its own key — that IS the status quo this thesis is arguing against. There is no actor-side signing step to time, so this is n/a rather than the '~0 Sek.' §24 currently prints. '0' would imply Design B does the same thing instantly; it does not do it at all.
the signing ceremony (Phase 5) is being built — client-side ES256K-R signing, attestation upload and verification, PendingAttestation staleness — and the operator-side signing UI does not exist yet
measurements.precondition: Phase 5 complete, then a headless-browser or instrumented-frontend timer from the sign action to the attestation being accepted by the upload route

measurements.reason: not run: this measurement MUTATES (each run freezes a new PassportVersion), so it is opt-in
measurements.notes: This is the closest Design B analogue to Design A's signing ceremony, but it is NOT the same quantity: it covers the platform signing the entire credential graph at once, not one actor signing one contribution. Compare with care, and only after saying so.

measurements.reason: this is a published LIST PRICE, not an observable quantity — no timer or receipt can produce it, and this harness will not scrape a vendor pricing page into a thesis table
measurements.precondition: --web3auth-usd-per-maw <rate>, cited in the thesis with the plan tier and the date read
measurements.notes: §13's RQ3 table promises this row. It is the recurring operational cost of Design A's key custody and it has no Design B counterpart (Design B holds its own key). Flagged so it is not silently dropped: it is the one RQ3 row that is answered by a citation rather than by this harness.

measurements.reason: Design B holds one platform key in its own infrastructure and buys no custody service, so there is no per-wallet fee. This asymmetry is a real finding — Design A trades a recurring vendor cost for the property that the platform cannot sign — and printing '0' would erase it.
